AutoExposureOut.description:
What *Auto uma vez* found (FR-ACQ-11). The camera is left on `value_us`; the editor writes it in the draft as a
fixed exposure.
AutoExposureOut.title: AutoExposureOut

BatchOut.description: The draft on all its samples (frontend.md §9.4): what feeds the dots of the gauges and the separation line.
BatchOut.title: BatchOut

BatchSampleOut.description: One picture of the draft's samples run through it: the reference, a *Boa*, a *Ruim* or one that should give ERROR.
BatchSampleOut.title: BatchSampleOut

CaseRunOut.description: One sample run through a draft: what the job said against what was expected (Validar, frontend.md §4.3).
CaseRunOut.title: CaseRunOut

ColourProposalOut.description: A color range for the color tool, from the pixels the person dragged over (FR-UI-13). OpenCV scales (hue 0..179).
ColourProposalOut.title: ColourProposalOut

CriterionOut.description: One check of a tool. `<tool type>.<code>` is its reason code when it fails.
CriterionOut.title: CriterionOut

CriterionSpecOut.description: One measure of a tool that has limits: what a tolerance gauge draws (frontend.md §9.3).
CriterionSpecOut.title: CriterionSpecOut

FixtureShape.description: A fixture as the editor draws it: its upright box, the pose and, when turned, the outline (architecture §14).
FixtureShape.title: FixtureShape

InspectionOut.description: An inspection another program asked for (FR-INT-1). `expired` means it never ran: treat it as an error.
InspectionOut.title: InspectionOut

JobDraft.description: A job being edited. Identity, version, author and date are set by the server on save.
JobDraft.title: JobDraft

JobVersionOut.description: One saved version, whole: what the editor opens.
JobVersionOut.title: JobVersionOut

LimitProposalOut.description: A limit the samples suggest for one side of one criterion of one tool (FR-UI-14).
LimitProposalOut.title: LimitProposalOut

LocateSampleOut.description: The fixtures of a draft on one picture of its reference set: where each was found, or why not (the anchor step).
LocateSampleOut.title: LocateSampleOut

Problem.description: Every error response: a message in the language of the request (Accept-Language), a machine code, and optional details.
Problem.title: Problem

ToolSeparationOut.description: How well one tool alone keeps the good samples apart from the bad ones.
ToolSeparationOut.title: ToolSeparationOut

TuneOut.description: A fine-tune saved as the next version, and what verifying it said. It is not active: the person activates it.
TuneOut.title: TuneOut

TypeInfo.description:
A tool or locator type the editor can offer, with the JSON Schema of its parameters. The schema carries
`x-level`, `x-group`, `x-widget`, `x-unit` and `x-tunable` on each parameter. `criteria` is empty for a locator.
TypeInfo.title: TypeInfo

VerifyOut.description: The draft on every sample of its reference set: the same run that activation does (design rule 4).
VerifyOut.title: VerifyOut

post.description:
Write these settings to the camera while watching the live view. The station is paused first; resuming
it (`POST /api/station/resume`) writes the active job's settings back.

*Auto uma vez*: find the exposure once, with the settings of this draft profile, and leave the camera on it.
The station is paused first, as in `/camera/apply`; the measuring parameters are the profile's
`exposure.auto_once`. It takes several seconds: the camera is written and settles at every step.
Images and labels for training, into <data>/exports/ (training happens offline, TD-08).

get.description: The images a job has in the dataset, newest first, for the grid with their labels (document 05 §7.5).
One image of the dataset, reduced to `width` (a grid of thumbnails does not carry full frames).

post.description:
The draft on all its samples at once (frontend.md §9.4). It feeds the dots of the tolerance gauges and the
separation line: nothing is saved or recorded, and the results are simulated.

Only the locating step of the draft on its reference picture and on every sample: where each fixture is found, with its
pose, or why it is not (frontend.md §7.3, step 3). Nothing is saved or recorded.
A color range from the pixels the person sampled on the image; the editor shows it as a proposal (FR-UI-13).

The limits the *Boa* and *Ruim* samples suggest for each criterion of each tool (FR-UI-14). Nothing is
changed: the editor shows each proposal and applies it only when the person says so.
Trigger an inspection and get an id to follow it (FR-INT-1). Only when the station is ready.

get.description: The request and, when done, its result. `wait_s` waits up to that many seconds for it.

post.description: A `.vjob` or a `.vbak`, as the raw request body. Stores new versions; activating is a separate, verified step.
Run a draft on the camera's newest frame (or a given image) without saving or activating it.
Check a draft without saving it: field errors, or why it could not run.

Run a draft on every sample of its reference set (Validar). It is the run activation does, so a draft that
passes here is not refused there for its samples; nothing is saved or recorded.
A new job (new id, version 1) from a saved version, with all its files.

Save a fine-tune as version n+1 and verify it (FR-JOB-14, document 05 §7.12). The draft is whatever the screen
built, and the server decides what may differ from the version it starts from: tolerance limits and new samples,
nothing else. A note is required. The version is not activated: that is the person's next step.

Save the draft as version n+1. The draft may start from any version (`draft.base`, where its files come
from), but the newest version it saw (`draft.latest`, else `draft.base`) must still be the latest: if
someone saved meanwhile, 409 instead of silently building on a version the editor did not see (VIA-0047).

Verify the job's decision logic on its reference set, record it as active and switch the station to it.
The camera part of the verification runs on the station itself (a failure shows as a fault on the screen).

get.description:
One file of a saved version (a reference image, a template), for the editor to show. `width` reduces an image
(the thumbnails of the filmstrip do not carry full frames).

post.description: The reference image and its measures from the live view (or an upload), to add to a draft.
A reference-set image, with what the draft says about it now (the editor records the expected result).

get.description: The reason codes in the results the other filters select, with how many each has: the options of the code filter.

post.description: The operator or supervisor says a result was wrong; the image becomes labeled training data (FR-MDL-2).

get.description: A recorded result's picture, smaller, for the operator screen's last results (everyone, frontend.md §7.1).

put.description:
The first password of the Maintainer, with no login: only while there is none, once, and only when the
API listens on this PC (anyone who can reach it from the network would otherwise take over the station).
No session is opened; the screen logs in afterwards. Everything after it asks for a login.

get.description: Whether the first password can be created now: for the notice on the operator screen. Says nothing else.

The seven steps of the wizard and whether the installation still needs it. Open to everyone while the
Maintainer has no password (the first step creates it); the Maintainer's afterwards.

put.description:
Save the system configuration. Recording limits, backups and the station's settings apply at once;
camera and network changes after a restart (`restart_required`).

post.description:
Open the camera described and wait for one frame. The camera the station is using is not opened a
second time (a USB camera serves one program): its current state is reported instead.

get.description: Tool and locator types with the JSON Schema of their parameters, for the editor's forms.

post.description: Manual (FR-TRG-3) and external (FR-TRG-2) trigger.
End every session, this one included.

put.description: The maintainer sets either password; a supervisor only their own, confirming the old one.
